Getting Started

Build your first Portal App application in minutes

{/* Main Content */}
{/* Installation Section */}
1

Installation

Get started with Portal App using the official scaffolding tool. This creates a new project with all dependencies configured.

$ npm create @interchained/portal@latest my-app
Creates a new Portal App project with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and routing pre-configured.
$ cd my-app
$ npm install
Install dependencies and you are ready to develop.
{/* Project Structure Section */}
2

Project Structure

Portal App uses file-based routing. Every file in the pages directory automatically becomes a route.

my-app/
├── pages/
├── index.tsx → /
├── about.tsx → /about
├── docs/
├── getting-started.tsx → /docs/getting-started
└── [id].tsx → /docs/:id
├── app.contract.ts
├── app.config.ts
└── package.json

Dynamic Routes: Use square brackets like [id].tsx for dynamic segments. Access params with useParams().

{/* App Contract Section */}
3

Define Your Contract

The app.contract.ts file defines your application's API schema and capabilities. This is where you declare all endpoints and their types. 

{`// app.contract.ts
import { defineContract } from '@interchained/portal-react';

export const appContract = defineContract({
  endpoints: {
    'GET /api/users': {
      response: { users: [{ id: 'string', name: 'string' }] }
    },
    'POST /api/users': {
      body: { name: 'string', email: 'string' },
      response: { id: 'string', created: true }
    },
    'GET /api/docs/:id': {
      params: { id: 'string' },
      response: { title: 'string', content: 'string' }
    }
  }
});`}

Type Safety: Your contract provides full TypeScript inference across your application. Use it in components and API calls for compile-time safety.

{/* Development Server Section */}
4

Start Development

Launch the development server with hot module reloading. Your changes appear instantly in the browser.

$ npm run dev
Server runs on http://localhost:3000 by default

Hot Reload

Edit files and see changes instantly without losing state.

Error Overlay

Build errors display in-browser with helpful diagnostics.

{/* Audit Section */}
5

Audit Your Application

Use the Portal App audit command to analyze your application structure, validate contracts, and check for common issues.

$ npm run audit
Validates routes, contracts, and configuration
✓

Route Validation

Checks all pages are properly exported and accessible

✓

Contract Integrity

Verifies endpoints match your app.contract.ts definitions

✓

Type Safety

Ensures all API calls match contract definitions

{/* First Component Section */}
6

Your First Component

Create a new page by adding a file to the pages directory. It will be automatically registered as a route. 

{`// pages/hello.tsx
export default function HelloPage() {
  return (
    

      
Hello from Portal App!

      
This page is available at /hello

    

  );
}`}
